analysis.one_liner: Asian Paints is India's largest paint company, making decorative and industrial paints plus home-decor and waterproofing products, now facing its most serious competitive challenge in decades.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (Jul-Sep 2026), declared 29 Oct 2026: revenue rose 17% YoY to ₹9,977 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.6% from 18% a year earlier - below the company's own 18-20% FY27 guidance - so net profit grew a slower 7.5% to ₹1,068 crore. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹5.75/share with a record date of 4 November 2026, just days away, payable on or after 13 November 2026. CEO Amit Syngle said competitive intensity has risen sharply.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the company behind the paint cans in almost every Indian hardware shop, and it used to earn best-in-class margins because it had scale and no serious rival. That changed when Aditya Birla Group's Birla Opus entered decorative paints in 2024 and has since grabbed roughly 7-10% of the market by undercutting on price and dealer margins. Asian Paints is still growing revenue, but it is giving up profitability to defend its position - margins are shrinking even as sales rise. Management says margins will recover to 18-20%, but that is a claim to watch, not assume.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026): revenue ₹9,977 crore, up 17% YoY, but domestic decorative volumes grew only 6.4% - meaning a meaningful part of revenue growth came from price/mix and international operations, not volumes alone. EBITDA rose just ~3.3-3.6% to roughly ₹1,534-1,557 crore, so EBITDA margin compressed to 15.6% from 18% a year ago. Net profit grew 7.5% to ₹1,068 crore - profit growth outpacing EBITDA growth suggests tax or other below-the-line items helped; worth checking the detailed P&L on Screener rather than reading profit growth as pure operating improvement. Management held its FY27 EBITDA margin guidance at 18-20%, a level the first half hasn't come close to.
analysis.performance_read: The 1-year return (-7.12%) actually beat the Nifty (-10.92%) and peer Berger Paints (-13.98%), but that is a case of a bad year being less bad than everyone else's. The multi-year picture is worse: the stock is down 20% over 3 years and 22% over 5 years while the Nifty gained 21% and 29% respectively - a rare and severe underperformance for a former blue-chip compounder. There is no recent corporate action distorting this (the stock's only splits were in 2003 and 2013, long settled); the -32.4% drawdown from the July 2023 peak of ₹3,430 is a genuine business-driven de-rating tied to the Birla Opus-led competitive squeeze, not a chart artifact.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 45x and a price-to-book of about 10x (₹2,320 price against a book value near ₹227), the stock is still priced like a premium compounder facing limited competition. Why it carries this multiple: a near-debt-free balance sheet, ROE near 22%, ROCE above 26%, and a long record of pricing power. Whether that multiple is justified now is the open question - a 45x P/E assumes margins recover toward the 18-20% guidance, which the last two quarters have not delivered.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently price/mix-led, not volume-led, in the core domestic decorative business - volumes grew just 6.4% while reported revenue grew 17%, with pricing and international operations filling the gap. That is the less durable combination, especially now that decorative paints is a structurally more price-competitive category than it was two years ago.
analysis.health_read: The balance sheet itself is clean - low debt (debt/equity near 0.18) and a steady dividend track record (TTM dividend ₹27.5/share). The risk here is not financial distress but business risk: a structural loss of pricing power and market share to a well-funded new entrant, which is already showing up as margin compression even as the top line keeps growing.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding has stayed stable at roughly 52.6% for several quarters - no sign of promoters exiting. But promoter pledging is notable: about 10.4% of promoter holdings were under pledge as of September 2026, including fresh pledge creation by promoter entity Smiti Holding and Trading Company. That is a watchpoint worth disclosing, not proof of distress. Institutional ownership is broad and conventional - FIIs near 13.8%, mutual funds (SBI MF and ICICI Prudential MF among the largest) near 9.9% - this is a standard large-cap institutional register, not one anchored by a single well-known individual investor.
strengths: ROCE of ~26% and ROE of ~22%, still well above most industrial peers despite margin pressure
Near debt-free balance sheet (debt/equity ~0.18), giving room to absorb a price war without financial strain
Domestic decorative volumes still grew 6.4% YoY in Q2 FY27, showing the core business hasn't shrunk
1-year stock return (-7.12%) held up better than both the Nifty and peer Berger Paints over the same period
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell to 15.6% in Q2 FY27 from 18% a year earlier, well short of the company's own 18-20% FY27 guidance
Birla Opus (Grasim) has grown to roughly 7-10% market share in decorative paints since its 2024 launch, and the CCI is reviewing a complaint it filed alleging anti-competitive conduct by Asian Paints
About 10.4% of promoter holding was under pledge as of September 2026, including fresh pledges by promoter entity Smiti Holding
Stock has underperformed the Nifty by roughly 40-50 percentage points over both 3 and 5 years, reflecting a steady market re-rating of the competitive risk
analysis.one_thing: Whether H2 FY27 EBITDA margin actually moves back toward the company's stated 18-20% guidance, or stays stuck near 15-16% under Birla Opus-led discounting - that outcome will settle whether the current ~45x P/E is justified.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) results across Business Standard, Upstox and other financial media - revenue (+17% YoY) and net profit (+7.5% YoY) were consistent; the EBITDA margin compression (15.6% vs 18% YoY) was corroborated by multiple outlets. P/E and P/B figures varied by source (P/E cited 36x-46x, P/B cited 5x-10x); used the computed P/B (price ₹2,320 ÷ book value ~₹227 ≈ 10.2x) and the more recent ~45x P/E as the more reliable reads, setting aside the lower, apparently stale figures. Promoter pledge quantum (~10.37% of promoter holding, Sept 2026) and the exact current shareholding split could not be independently re-verified on Screener/BSE within this session - treat as approximate and check on Screener for the latest filing.
